match.reason: The bank point 'Casual and gig work' covers casual employment as well as gig work, so it is broader than the gig economy point, and its questions test casual pay rather than app-based gig work, while the brief's point about missing super is not in it, so a new point is the safer match.

draft.title: The gig economy
card: The gig economy is a way of working where people do short jobs, called gigs, that they find through an app or website. Food delivery and ride sharing are common examples.
Gig workers can often choose when they work and how many gigs they take. This flexibility suits people who want to fit work around study, family or other jobs.
Gig work often lacks steady pay. Workers may be paid for each gig, so their income can rise and fall from week to week.
Gig workers are often not given paid leave, such as sick leave or holiday pay. Their super may also be missing or small, unless they arrange it themselves.
draft.remember: Gig work trades flexibility for less certainty about pay, leave and super.

a.q: Which of these is the best example of work in the gig economy?
opts: Taking food delivery jobs through an app when you choose
Working fixed shifts each week at a supermarket
Running a shop that has staff on set wages
Working a full-time office job with paid holidays
a.why: A gig is a short job found through an app, and the worker picks which ones to take. Fixed supermarket shifts are regular work with a set roster, so they are not gigs, even though the work is part-time.
a.clue: Look for short jobs found through an app.

b.q: Sam drives for a ride-sharing app in Geelong and is paid for each trip. In a quiet week he gets few bookings and earns much less. Which feature of gig work does this show?
opts: Pay that is not steady from week to week
A lack of choice about when to work
Having no paid work at all
Being paid a fixed wage whatever the demand
b.why: Sam is paid for each trip, so his income follows how many trips he gets. That makes his pay unsteady. Choosing his own hours is a different feature of gig work, and it is not what the quiet week shows.
b.clue: Think about what happens to pay when there are fewer trips.

a.best: Taking food delivery jobs through an app when you choose

b.best: Pay that is not steady from week to week

problems.detail: Why (a) says the supermarket work is part-time ('even though the work is part-time'), but the option only says fixed weekly shifts and never mentions part-time. This could confuse students.
